note: Productive tensions / contested or qualified positions in Design for Dasein (Wendt-says). Each edge records where Wendt pushes against, corrects, or qualifies a source or a common design position. Faithful (not anticipatory-application).

tensions.wendt_position: The interface is an active mediation and a moving concentration of affordances, NOT the designer's 'central domain'.
tensions.against: Gui Bonsiepe (interface as central domain / the deliverable)
tensions.note: Fetishizing the interface forgets user behavior/variability and what happens after design; sustains a dualist, positivist (Simon) inner/outer illusion.

tensions.wendt_position: Designers CAN design at the level of systems and influence how a thing 'things'; the object also 'things on its own' with multistable tendencies.
tensions.note: Heidegger 'forgets' systems-level design and the object's own multistable agency — exactly where experience designers work.

tensions.wendt_position: Background relations are a matter of proximity and direct involvement, not (only) of conscious awareness; experience is shaped by conscious AND non-conscious factors.
tensions.against: Peter-Paul Verbeek (background relations defined by lack of conscious awareness)
tensions.note: Wendt calls the awareness-only criterion 'unnecessarily restrictive'.

tensions.wendt_position: Use is necessary for sense but can be distinct from meaning; meaning is not simply 'secondary to use'.
tensions.note: We know a tank's meaning without operating one, though it makes little sense to us.

tensions.wendt_position: Transparency (perceived-through, can move in and out of awareness) is the attainable, preferable design goal; 'invisibility'/'intuition' is inaccurate and potentially harmful.
tensions.against: the invisible-/intuitive-interface ideal (incl. Mark Weiser's calm computing; Michael May's reliance argument)
tensions.note: The invisibility ideal harbors Ihde's contradictory 'double desire' and Heidegger's fear of a docile Dasein (standing reserve).

tensions.wendt_position: The early tool-analysis (ready-to-hand/withdrawal) sits in tension with late Heidegger's near-Platonic 'essence of technology'.
tensions.note: Wendt works mostly from the early, design-usable Heidegger while acknowledging the Turn.

tensions.wendt_position: Technological objects are not isolated solutions to discrete problems — but the strong evolutionary claim is 'a bit extreme'.
tensions.note: Adopts the systems/holism point while distancing from full technological-evolutionism.

tensions.wendt_position: Cross's 'design phenomenology' (form/configuration of artefacts) is too narrow and actually encompasses design epistemology and praxiology.
tensions.against: Nigel Cross (three facets of design research)
tensions.note: Because artefacts embody our understanding of the world, the 'phenomenology' facet subsumes the other two.

tensions.wendt_position: The 'unicorn' pure-generalist designer is ill-equipped for complex projects; specialization preserves care.
tensions.against: unicornism (the maker-generalist ideal of lean startups)
tensions.note: Division of labor is both strength and Achilles' heel; care erodes when spread thin (echoed dfd-06).

tensions.wendt_position: Designer intention is not primary and is effectively irrelevant once a product launches; outcomes are emergent.
tensions.note: Ihde's designer fallacy (parallel to Wimsatt & Beardsley's intentional fallacy); launch is a step toward understanding, not the end of design.

tensions.wendt_position: The problem-solution 'dichotomy' is not a dichotomy except under strict dualism; the paradox is an antinomy to be redefined, not a linear sequence to be resolved.
tensions.note: Problems and solutions co-evolve (Dorst); 'solutionism' manufactures problems for profit.

tensions.wendt_position: 'Don't make me think' / delegation can wrongly strip agency from the human actant and offload moral responsibility onto objects.
tensions.against: the frictionless-UX mantra ('don't make me think')
tensions.note: Delegation (speed bump, weighted hotel key, automatic seat belt) has an ethics; ties to transparency-not-invisibility.
